In [earlier posts](https://agrogan1.github.io/blog.html#category=exploring%20data), I have been looking at different ways to get an idea of what *scales* and *demographic* variables in my data are related to other *scales* and *demographic* variables in my data. 

In [a post from a while back](../what-is-related-to-what), I looked at `corrgram`s [@corrgram]. I think that there are many ways to explore data visually, but have come to like the simplicity of both the code for `corrgram`s, and the visual presentation of `corrgram`s for many purposes.

Here is a `corrgram` using the the data from [a post on making a network graph](../network-graph/).

```{r}

load("../network-graph/mydata.RData")

```

```{r}

library(corrgram) # corrgrams

corrgram(mydata, 
         order=TRUE, 
         lower.panel = panel.pie, # lower panel is pie charts
         upper.panel = panel.cor, # upper panel is correlations
         text.panel = panel.txt, # text panel is variable
         diag.panel=panel.minmax, # minimum and maximum
         main = "Correlation of Scales in Our Data") 

```
